summary: The session discusses the relationship between business intelligence (BI) and decision intelligence (DI), emphasizing that DI is not merely an evolution of BI but a distinct discipline focused on improving decision-making outcomes. It highlights the importance of integrating AI into decision-making processes to enhance efficiency and reduce reliance on traditional BI tools. The speaker also addresses the need for organizations to adopt a decision-centric approach to leverage both BI and DI effectively.

key_points: Decision intelligence is distinct from business intelligence and focuses on decision-making outcomes.
The session will explore the integration of AI in decision-making processes.
Decision intelligence is a practical discipline that enhances decision-making by understanding how decisions are made.
It includes decision modeling and the orchestration of decision workflows.
There are three decision-making models: decision support, decision augmentation, and decision automation.
Decision intelligence platforms can facilitate all three models.
Business intelligence often lacks real-time context and can be difficult to connect to decision-making.
Adoption of BI tools has stagnated despite advancements in technology.
A synergistic relationship between BI and DI can enhance decision-making capabilities.
Real-time context and advanced analytics are crucial for effective integration.
The future will see more automation and augmentation in decision-making processes.
Organizations should focus on incremental adoption of decision intelligence.

key_takeaways: Organizations must shift from a data-driven to a decision-centric approach to improve outcomes.
Integrating AI into decision-making processes can enhance efficiency and reduce reliance on traditional BI tools.
Incremental adoption of decision intelligence is crucial to mitigate risks associated with rapid changes.
